findings.reason: the plan should either keep the single-pass boundary walk or state the concrete boundary contract the two parsers share (including heading retention inside a card), instead of describing a cross-module two-parse coupling as "the counters ... deleted".
findings.text: §16 says `_AuthoredProseParser` "takes its section boundaries from" §17's raw-text reader and deletes the `_card_depth`/`_heading_depth`/`_section_is_card` counters, but those counters are a single-pass streaming walk (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:162-259`) over the document, while `_StructuredSectionSpanParser` (`reckon/_plan_html.py:44`) is a separate parser over the same text; the change turns one streaming pass into a two-parser, offset-join dependency across two modules, and the card-span yield cannot by itself preserve the heading inside a landed card while dropping the card's interior, which is exactly what the counters do

findings.reason: §17 must name the full set of store helpers that fold into the parser (the close-balancer and the section regexes), or the consolidation leaves section extent under two owners and adds the cross-module private import the house rule §16 and §18 state forbids.
findings.text: §17 moves `_landed_card_span` and `_is_structural_boundary` into the parser, but `_landed_card_span` recognises a card by calling `_matching_section_close` (`reckon/_store.py:950`) and `_SECTION_OPEN_RE`/`_SECTION_CLOSE_RE` (`reckon/_store.py:808`), none of which §17 names, so those stay owned by the store while their only card-span caller moves to `reckon/_plan_html.py`, leaving card/section-extent recognition with two owners and the parser importing the store's private balancer

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §16 removes `_AuthoredProseParser`'s own section/card boundary tracking and sources those boundaries from a second parser in another module, splitting the fingerprint's authored-content behaviour across `reckon/crew/plan_review.py` and `reckon/_plan_html.py` behind what it presents as a simplification.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §17 names only `_landed_card_span` and `_is_structural_boundary` as folding into the parser, leaving their dependencies on card/extent recognition owned by `reckon/_store.py`, so section-extent recognition keeps a second owner.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1476, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 adds no public definition and retires the public `legacy` parameter of `plan_fingerprint`, §17 and §18 each add exactly one public definition and each names in its own text the private walks/name it retires, so no section adds to a family without accounting for it.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the design searches the code it extends and cites the mechanisms it reuses: §16 names `_fingerprint_forms` (`reckon/crew/plan_review.py:598`) and `landed_section_ids` (`reckon/_store.py:1034`), §17 names `_StructuredSectionSpanParser` (`reckon/_plan_html.py:44`) and its thirteen heading-walk sites, §18 names `promotion._plan_remaining_sections` (`reckon/crew/promotion.py:7236`) and `doccheck._implementable_section_ids` (`reckon/doccheck.py:1014`); every named mechanism exists.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §18 is a hoist of an existing reader (move, not a new layer), §17 extends the existing parser rather than wrapping it, and no proposed layer forwards to existing machinery without a stated reason.
